title: Surge sinewave latency + cost brief
body:
Executive summary:

We ran a small-series benchmark to quantify latency and per-query cost behavior under a smooth, repeated surge pattern (sinewave traffic) rather than single-shot spikes. Goal: understand how pacing/slot allocation + KV cache hygiene affect p50/p90/p99 during predictable oscillatory load, and estimate incremental $/q during the crest windows.

Key takeaways:
- Under a 30s-period sinewave (QPS oscillates between 20 and 220, mean ~120), p50 stayed acceptable (~40–60ms) except during crest ramp where it rose to ~240ms. p90 and p99 show the largest sensitivity: p90 up ~3.2x baseline during crests, p99 up ~7x.
- Cost per successful query (amortized GPU-minute + infra) increases by ~28% during high-phase vs baseline, but effective cost per token over a full period is only +6% due to smoothing gains during troughs (opportunity to consolidate).
- Prefetching + thin prewarmed slots reduced p90 by ~18% during crests with only +4% steady-state cost.

Experiment design and motivation:
- Motivation: many customer workloads are periodic (polling, notification checks, scheduled enrichments). A sinewave captures repeated crests/decays and reveals hysteresis in slot allocation, cache warmup, and preemption effects.
- Traffic generator: synthetic client that issues chat-turn sized requests (avg 120 tokens). Waveform: sin(2πt/T) scaled to QPS in [20,220], T=30s. Duration: 90 minutes per run (180 cycles). Warmup: 60s steady at mean QPS.
- Models/hardware: small test model (redwood-7B-quant8) on A100-40GB dedicated pool (16 GPUs, each node runs 64 multiplex slots baseline).
- Configs compared: baseline (opportunistic multiplex, no prefetch), prewarm-thin (2 prewarmed slots per node), prefetch-kv (aggressive KV cache retention between sessions), hybrid (prewarm + prefetch).
- Metrics collected: qps (observed), p50/p90/p99 latency, tail-service-time, slot-occupancy, KV cache hit%, GPU utilization, cost (GPU-minutes prorated + infra).

ASCII waveform summary (one period sample):
Time(s):    0   5  10  15  20  25  30
QPS         120  160 200 220 200 160 120

Representative latency snapshots (ms) - baseline:
Period phase: trough | ramp-up | crest | ramp-down
QPS approx   : 20    | 80      | 220   | 80
p50          : 38    | 55      | 240   | 62
p90          : 85    | 140     | 680   | 160
p99          : 210   | 420     | 1500  | 520

Representative latency snapshots (ms) - prewarm-thin:
p50          : 36    | 48      | 190   | 56
p90          : 78    | 110     | 560   | 130
p99          : 190   | 360     | 1200  | 430

Cost estimates (dollars) - simplified model:
- Assumptions: GPU cost $3.60 / GPU-hour (effective blended rate), infra overhead + networking = 15% of GPU cost, amortization across slots per-node by occupancy. Billing bucket = GPU-minutes used by active slots + prewarm overhead.
- Baseline run: average utilization 62% across nodes -> effective cost per 1000 queries = $0.76
- During crest (QPS>180): incremental GPU-minute consumption + preemption caused utilization jump to 95% -> crest 1000-queries cost = $0.98 (+28%)
- Prewarm-thin: baseline steady-state cost = $0.79 (+4%); crest cost per 1000 queries = $0.86 (+7% over prewarm baseline, -12% vs baseline crest)

Compact sensitivity table (observed):
Config        | mean util | p99 mean | cost/1kq (avg)
--------------|-----------|----------|---------------
Baseline      | 62%       | 400 ms   | $0.76
Prewarm-thin  | 65%       | 360 ms   | $0.79
Prefetch-kv   | 60%       | 320 ms   | $0.81
Hybrid        | 67%       | 300 ms   | $0.85

Observations and interpretation:
- Hysteresis matters: allocation slow-path and slot cold-starts create a pronounced tail during crest onset. The waveform reveals a lagged p99 peak ~6–9s after QPS peak due to queue backfills and decode churn.
- Prefetch vs prewarm trade: prefetch reduces tail by improving model KV hit rate (faster decode per token), prewarm reduces allocation latency (fewer slot cold starts). Hybrid is best at latency but highest steady-state cost.
- Smoothing wins: when crest frequency is moderate (T >= 20s), the platform can amortize bursts by temporarily increasing batching; very short periods (<5s) behave like random microbursts and are much harder to optimize without extra slot cushion.

Recommendations (engineer-facing):
1) For customers with periodic surges T in [20s, 90s], provide a "sinewave-friendly" policy: thin prewarm (config toggle) + adaptive KV hold for session tokens. Default prewarm 2 slots/node for Dedicated pools.
2) Expose a pacing hint in the API (client-side) that lets us align prefetch window with expected crest times (e.g., scheduled pushes).
3) Implement a short-lived slot-burst cache: keep recently evicted slots in a ready pool for 10s to cut start penalty. Low complexity and low memory cost; we saw ~12–20% p90 reduction in trials.
4) Add a console plot type: rolling-waveform overlay (QPS and p99) to help customers detect periodicity and recommend knob presets.

Action items / next experiments:
- PLAT-4021: A/B test prewarm=1/2/4 slots/node across more model families (7B, 13B) to measure slope changes. (owner: Ravi)
- Measure very-short T (<8s) microburst behavior with priority-preemption on a limited cluster to evaluate if slot-burst cache helps (owner: Maya)
- Cost modeling: refine infra overhead assumptions with finance (ticket: FIN-771) and add bandwidth-sensitive scenarios for mobile-heavy payloads (owner: Sofia)

Appendix: reproducibility notes:
- Client and workload generator are in github: pr/1137, run with --waveform sine --period 30 --qmin 20 --qmax 220 --duration 5400
- Use per-node logs (slot events) + telemetry aggregator for KV hit traces at 100ms granularity. Sampling used: 1:100 for full traces.
- Raw CSV exports attached to Confluence page confluence:PLAT-Surge-SineWave-2027 (charts and full tables).

Questions / open items:
- What is the acceptable p99 budget for PLG customers vs SLA customers under periodic surges? We need policy thresholds to trigger hybrid prewarm automatically.
- Is a 10s slot-burst cache operationally safe at scale given memory constraints? Small pilot recommended.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a draft focused on the platform-level knobs for periodic surges. Please focus feedback on the practicality of adding a slot-burst cache and the prewarm defaults.
summary: Draft benchmark + recommendations for handling periodic surge (sinewave) traffic. Compares baseline vs prewarm/prefetch/hybrid; highlights latency tails and cost delta; recommends thin prewarm + slot-burst cache and new console visualization.
